images.seen: An empty bed with the duvet thrown back into a body-shaped tunnel, grey misty winter morning and bare branches through the window. Friday.
lines: The warmest place in the province was abandoned here at about six-fifteen.
The window says mist and bare branches; the bed rests its case.

images.seen: An SUV with its windscreen completely frosted over in fern patterns, lit gold by the rising sun, frosty brown lawn and a modern double-storey house. Sunday.
lines: Minus something this morning: the windscreen has grown its own art collection.
The first ten minutes of this Sunday belong to a credit card and the demister.
Frost on the grass, ferns on the glass — the night went well below zero here.

images.seen: A toddler peeking out of a duvet cave built on the lounge floor, lamp glowing, a gloomy grey winter day through the window. Friday.
lines: Construction finished at nine: one duvet cave, single occupant, no visitors till spring.
The day outside never got light properly, so the day inside went underground.

images.seen: A man in a beanie and jacket walking a small dog in a knitted jersey along a wet road in drizzle, grey estate street. Monday.
lines: Both of them are dressed for this, and neither is pretending to enjoy it.
Wet road, grey sky, dog in a jersey: winter is fully operational.
Cold like this turns the morning walk into an errand.
